name: Southwest Scramble

waypoints.name: Snow Lakes Trailhead
waypoints.note: 4.2 mi south on Icicle Creek Rd (FR-76) from junction with US-2, Leavenworth.
waypoints.directions: From Leavenworth, follow Icicle Road (Forest Road 7600) about 4.2 to 4.3 miles to the Snow Lakes Trailhead, at roughly 1,350 feet. Park in the lot on the south side of the road at the trailhead.

waypoints.name: Nada Lake
waypoints.directions: Snow Lakes Trail #1553 crosses Icicle Creek and climbs steadily through forest up the Snow Creek drainage on long, relentless switchbacks to Nada Lake, with a loud creek just above it that is a reliable water source.

waypoints.name: Snow Lakes basin
waypoints.directions: Continue past Nada Lake to Lower and Upper Snow Lakes. The crossing on the logjam between the two lakes is the known hazard here, worst at high water or on a pre-dawn start.

waypoints.name: Base of southwest slopes
waypoints.directions: Above the Snow Lakes the tread becomes a rougher climbers' path that switchbacks steeply into the core Enchantments basin past Lake Viviane to Leprechaun Lake, near 7,000 ft. Leave the trail at the flat, open ground by Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes; there is no reliable water beyond the lakes.

waypoints.name: McClellan Peak summit
waypoints.directions: Climb steep talus, scree or snow, often firm and icy late in the season, to the crest of McClellan Ridge, keeping west of the rock tower called the Prong; drifting farther west into the Chessman towers dead-ends. From the crest, drop a short way and wrap onto the south side of the peak, then scramble Class 3 rock to the summit.

approach: From Leavenworth, drive Icicle Road (Forest Road 7600) about 4.2–4.3 miles west to the Snow Lakes Trailhead and parking area on the south side of the road (~1,350 ft). Start on the Snow Lakes Trail No. 1553, which climbs steadily through forest along Icicle Creek/Snow Creek drainage. Around 4 miles in you pass Nada Lake, with a loud waterfall/creek blast just above it that's a reliable water source; continue to Lower and Upper Snow Lakes, where a logjam between the two lakes is a known crossing hazard (especially at high water or in the dark on an alpine start). Beyond the Snow Lakes the trail (now a rougher climbers' path) switchbacks steeply up into the core Enchantments basin, passing Lake Viviane, then Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes — by this point you've covered roughly 9–10 miles and gained most of the route's elevation. At the flat, open area at ~7,000 ft between Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes, leave the maintained trail and head south-southeast, aiming for McClellan Ridge and staying west of a distinctive rock tower known as "the Prong." Ascend steep talus, scree, or snow (depending on season — often firm/icy in late summer and fall, so an axe/microspikes are worth carrying) to gain the ridge crest. This upper section has no reliable water and involves real route-finding; a permit is required to camp overnight in the core Enchantments zone (May 15-Oct 31).

approach_variants.name: Snow Lakes to the core basin, then McClellan Ridge past the Prong
approach_variants.notes:
Snow Lakes Trailhead on Icicle Road about 4.2 miles from Leavenworth. Snow Lakes Trail #1553 climbs steadily through forest, passing Nada Lake at roughly 4 miles, then Lower and Upper Snow Lakes — the logjam between the two lakes is the known crossing hazard, especially at high water or on a pre-dawn start.

Above the Snow Lakes the tread coarsens into a climbers' path and switchbacks steeply into the core basin past Lake Viviane, then Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes. By this point most of the day's elevation is behind you.

Leave the trail at the flat, open ground around 7,000 ft between Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes and head south-southeast for McClellan Ridge.
approach_variants.season: Jul-Sep; late-season the slope below the ridge often goes icy
hazards: The logjam crossing between Lower and Upper Snow Lakes, worst at high water or in the dark
Steep snow below the ridge that turns firm and icy in late season — an axe or microspikes are worth carrying
Loose talus and scree gaining the ridge
No water above the basin lakes
Real route-finding with no trail on the upper half
approach_variants.baseFinding:
Two features decide this route and both are recorded errors.

First, the Prong: a distinct rock tower standing on the ground above you. The line keeps west of it, climbing steep talus, scree or snow to gain the ridge crest. Parties who drift the other way, west into the jumbled cluster of towers called the Chessman, report dead-ending in impassable ground and having to traverse back north to find the correct line.

Second, and this is the one that costs people the summit: once you are on McClellan Ridge, do not start up the first thing above you. Scramble east along the south side of the ridge and keep going around until you are on the southeast side of the summit block. From there it is an easy class 3 scramble that needs no thought.

The test is your first move. If it is a tricky slab followed by a chimney, you are on the southwest side and have stopped short — a few more minutes around to the southeast turns the same summit into a walk-up. Parties have also gained the crest and had to drop about seventy vertical feet before wrapping round to the south side.

No reliable water past the lakes in the basin, and no water at all on the upper section.

descent_text: This route's crux move is on the ridge itself, not a technical descent: from the ridge crest (reached via the ascent line west of the Prong), drop roughly 70 vertical feet off the crest and wrap around to the south side of McClellan Peak, then scramble up class 3 rock to the true summit — the "southwest scramble" line. Descend by reversing this exact sequence: downclimb the class 3 south-side rock back to the ~70-ft notch below the ridge crest, regain the crest, and drop back down the steep talus/scree/snow slope west of the Prong to the flat area between Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes at ~7,000 ft. From there, rejoin the Snow Lakes Trail (No. 1553) and retrace it past Lake Viviane, the Snow Lakes, and Nada Lake back to the trailhead — summit-to-trailhead typically takes roughly 5–5.5 hours. This is a walk-off/downclimb with no rappelling required. Watch for loose rock and exposure on the class 3 downclimb (parties have noted going down 20 ft and wrapping to an easier gully when the direct line felt too exposed), ice on the ridge slope in late season, and the same logjam crossing between the Snow Lakes on the way out. Carry an axe/microspikes if snow lingers on the upper slope, since a slip there has real runout consequences.
beta: From the Snow Lakes Trailhead, climb past Nada Lake and the Snow Lakes and on past Lake Viviane to the flat ground between Leprechaun and Sprite Lakes (~7,000 ft). Leave the trail there and head south-southeast toward the ridge connecting to McClellan, keeping west of the distinct rock tower known as 'The Prong.' Gain the ridge on Class 2-3 talus/slabs, cross to the south side, and finish with a short, exposed Class 3 (some report low Class 4) scramble up the summit block's SW side. Descend via an easier Class 2-3 line on the block's south/east side.
